title: Jerry Tubbs: Unanimous 1956 All-American Center at OU
question: Which Oklahoma center was a unanimous All-American in 1956 and finished fourth for the Heisman?
answer: Jerry Tubbs, who played for Oklahoma from 1954 to 1956, was a unanimous All-America center in 1956 and finished fourth in that year's Heisman Trophy voting. He was inducted into the College Football Hall of Fame in 1996.
summary: Jerry Tubbs moved from fullback to center under Bud Wilkinson, played on 31 straight OU wins, and became a unanimous 1956 All-American and Hall of Famer.
body: Jerry Tubbs came to Norman from Breckenridge, Texas, and played at Oklahoma from 1954 through 1956. He began as a fullback, averaging six yards per carry in 1954, before Bud Wilkinson moved him to center in 1955. That position became his signature, though he also played linebacker as a two-way starter.
He wasted no time making an impression on defense. In the 1955 game against Texas he intercepted three passes, a rare feat for a man who spent his plays snapping the ball on offense.

The teams around him were remarkable. Oklahoma went 10-0 in 1954, 11-0 in 1955 and 10-0 in 1956. The 1955 and 1956 squads were national champions, and the 1955 team beat Maryland 20-6 in the Orange Bowl, the only bowl game of his career.

In 1956 Tubbs was a unanimous All-America center, was named lineman of the year by three agencies, and was an Academic All-American with a degree in economics. He finished fourth in the Heisman Trophy voting, a high placement for an interior lineman.

The pro game kept him busy for years. He played linebacker from 1957 through 1967 for the Chicago Cardinals, San Francisco 49ers and Dallas Cowboys, then spent 21 years as a Cowboys assistant coach. The College Football Hall of Fame inducted him in 1996, and he died in 2012.
